text.p: Kuwait's 1996 provisional gross domestic product (GDP) at current prices grew 16.8 percent to 9.277 billion dinars ($30.7 billion), an official said on Monday.
"According to provisional figures, GDP for 1996 is 9.277 billion dinars," the official said.
The figure overshot estimates by independent economists who expected GDP to rise to around 8.7 billion dinars from a provisional 7.9 billion in 1995.
A rise of 31.6 percent for oil revenue was the main reason for the overall increase, the official said. Oil revenue grew by 10.8 percent in 1995.
According to figures, provisional for both 1996 and 1995, revenues from crude oil and natural gas reached 4.127 billion dinars in 1996 from 3.137 billion.
The refining industry's contribution to GDP rose to 716.8 million dinars from 580.6 million in 1995. Kuwait's OPEC quota is currently two million barrels per day, unchanged from 1996 and 1995.
Output from the non-oil sector rose by seven percent in 1996 to 5.247 billion dinars. Gross National Product (GNP) by current prices rose 15.1 percent to 10.749 billion dinars.
Cash transferred abroad rose to 504 million dinars from 496 million in 1995. Kuwait has a population of some 1.25 million foreigners and 710,000 Kuwaitis.
National disposable income also rose to 9.711 billion dinars in 1996 from 8.261 billion in 1995 and an actual 7.166 billion the year before that.
Net factor income from abroad rose 5.5 percent to 1.427 billion dinars. Per capita GDP rose to 5,289 dinars from 4,698 and per capita national income rose to 5,824 from 5,180.
Figures in million dinars unless stated
